title: Sourdough Pizza Crusts: Scoop for Even Mini Pizzas
meta_description: Stop guessing your dough portions! Learn how to use a cookie scoop for sourdough pizza crusts to get perfectly uniform mini pizzas every time.
html:
There is nothing more frustrating than putting a tray of mini sourdough pizzas in the oven only to find that three are burnt crisps while two others are still doughy in the middle. When you're working with a wild yeast starter, the hydration can make the dough sticky and unpredictable, making it a pain to divide by hand.

I discovered a game-changer in my own kitchen: using a cookie scoop sourdough pizza crusts method. By treating your pizza dough like cookie dough, you ensure every single mini pizza is the exact same weight and volume. This means consistent bake times and a professional look that makes your home-cooked meal feel like a gourmet appetizer platter.

Why Use a Cookie Scoop for Sourdough Pizza Crusts?

Sourdough is notoriously tacky. If you try to divide a bulk-fermented dough using a knife or bench scraper, you often end up with uneven pieces and a mess of flour all over your counter. A spring-release scoop allows you to portion the dough without over-handling it, which preserves those precious air bubbles (the crumb) that make sourdough so light.

Using a Cookie Dough Scoop eliminates the need for a kitchen scale for every single portion. Once you know which scoop size yields your desired pizza diameter, you can fly through a batch of ten or twenty mini crusts in a fraction of the time.

Choosing the Right Scoop Size

Not all scoops are created equal. Depending on whether you want bite-sized snacks or personal-sized mini pizzas, you'll need to pick the right volume. For most mini pizzas, a medium-to-large scoop is ideal. The Cookie Dough Scoop is particularly useful here because it offers spring-release options in various sizes, letting you scale your recipe up or down.

For a standard 4-inch mini pizza, look for a scoop that holds about 3 to 4 tablespoons of dough. If you are making "pizza bites" for a party, a smaller scoop (around 1.5 tablespoons) works best. This uniformity is the secret to achieving that perfect golden-brown edge across the entire batch.

Step-by-Step: Portioning Your Sourdough Dough

To get the best results, make sure your sourdough has completed its bulk fermentation and is nice and bubbly. Here is how to handle the process:

  • Prep your surface: Lightly flour your workspace or use a piece of parchment paper.
  • The Scoop: Dip the Cookie Dough Scoop into your dough. Press firmly to ensure the scoop is full and the dough is released cleanly by the spring mechanism.
  • The Drop: Drop the dough ball directly onto your baking sheet or a floured surface.
  • The Flatten: Use your thumb or a small rolling pin to press the ball into a disc. Because the portions are identical, they will all flatten to the same thickness.
  • The Topping: Add your sauce and cheese, being careful not to overload the center, which can lead to soggy crusts.

Tips for the Perfect Mini Pizza Bake

Since you've used a cookie scoop for sourdough pizza crusts to ensure size consistency, you can now optimize your oven settings. For the best crust, use a preheated baking stone or a flipped-over baking sheet. This mimics a pizza oven by delivering a burst of heat to the bottom of the dough.

Keep an eye on your oven's hot spots. Even with uniform dough, some ovens bake faster in the back. Rotate your tray halfway through the bake. Because the thickness is consistent thanks to the scoop, you won't have to worry about some pizzas being undercooked while others are overdone.

Storage and Freezing Sourdough Portions

One of the best parts of this method is meal prepping. You can use your Cookie Dough Scoop to portion out your sourdough dough and freeze the balls individually on a parchment-lined tray. Once frozen solid, pop them into a freezer bag.

When you're ready for a quick dinner, just thaw a few balls in the fridge overnight. Since they were scooped to a precise size, you already know exactly how many will fit on your tray and exactly how long they need to bake, taking the guesswork out of a weeknight meal.

FAQ

Can I use this method with high-hydration sourdough?

Yes, but it helps to lightly grease the inside of the scoop with a tiny bit of olive oil or a spray of non-stick cooking spray. This ensures the sticky dough releases cleanly every time.

Does using a scoop affect the rise of the pizza?

Not at all. In fact, it reduces the amount of degassing that happens when you manually chop and shape the dough with your hands, which can actually help you maintain a lighter, airier crust.

Which size scoop is best for a 6-inch personal pizza?

For a 6-inch pizza, you'll want a larger scoop or perhaps two medium scoops per pizza. Generally, a scoop that holds about 1/2 cup of dough is the sweet spot for a small personal-sized crust.
